newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES DROPS OUT OF NUMBER ONE RANKING.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES DROPS OUT OF NUMBER ONE RANKING.

text.p: Monica Seles, a surprise semifinals loser to Jennifer Capriati last weekend in Chicago, dropped out of a shared world number one ranking Monday for the first time since returning to tennis in the summer of 1995.
The Chicago result left Germany's Steffi Graf alone atop the Corel WTA Tour rankings. Seles fell to a co-ranking of number two with Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain.

When Seles ended her absence from the tour following the 1993 stabbing attack against her in Hamburg, the tour agreed to rank her co-number one for six events and then average her results for 18 months or 14 tournaments for a shared ranking.

The Yugoslav-born American was able to maintain her lofty status through her subsequent results, including victory at the Australian Open, but the semifinal loss in the Tier II Chicago event to 50th-ranked Capriati dropped her below Graf.
Seles, however, can climb back into a share of the top spot by winning this week's Bank of the West Classic in Oakland, California.
